content.text:
The Sea Keeps Its Own Counsel

It rises before the light is awake,
a grey breath moving under the dark,
and lays its wages on the sand
one white shell at a time.

I have stood at its edge and asked it things.
It answers in the grammar of waves,
each one a sentence that begins
and ends before I can finish reading.

It remembers everything it has touched:
the ships that went down singing,
the glass bottles carrying letters
to people who were already gone,
the children who waded out past their courage
and came back changed.

It does not hurry. It has no need to.
The moon pulls, and it answers.
The wind scrapes, and it shivers into lines.
Even its silences are full of motion.

Some days it is glass, so still
you could walk out on the reflected sky.
Other days it throws itself at the rocks
as though it had a grief it could not carry
and would rather break than hold.

I used to think it was indifferent.
Now I think it is only patient,
a vast and salted mind
that has learned the shape of every shore
and is in no rush to be understood.

So I come back, again and again,
to hear what it will not say.
The tide turns. The gulls go quiet.
The sea keeps its own counsel,
and I am glad of the company.
